I noduli subsolidi si dividono in puri a:
Subsolid nodules are divided into pure ground-glass and part-solid. A subsolid nodule that persists after a few months (infectious forms regress) is often an adenocarcinoma of the lepidic spectrum: from atypical adenomatous hyperplasia to adenocarcinoma in situ, minimally invasive and invasive adenocarcinoma.
The solid component generally corresponds to the invasive part: for the T stage the solid component is measured, not the total diameter (TNM 8th edition). Here the solid component is under 1 cm: cT1a (or cT1mi if ≤ 5 mm), even if the whole nodule exceeds 2 cm.
Management (Fleischner 2017, single part-solid nodules ≥ 6 mm): follow-up at 3-6 months to confirm persistence; if it persists and the solid component is ≥ 6 mm, suspicion is high and the path leads to PET-CT (poorly sensitive in ground-glass forms), biopsy or resection.
In the report: total diameter and diameter of the solid component (in lung window, on thin slices), location, margins, relationship with the pleura and fissures.
Nodulo subsolido persistente: il T si mi: Persistent subsolid nodule: the T is measured on the solid component.
Resezione 5 giorni dopo la TC: adenocarc: Resection 5 days after the CT: well-differentiated adenocarcinoma (G1), pT1a N0 M0, ground-glass component 75-100% (clinical data from the NSCLC-Radiogenomics collection).
